text: Infectious Bronchitis (IB) is caused by a virus and is considered the most contagious poultry disease known, spreading by air, visitors, feed bags, infected dead birds, and rodents; it affects only chickens. Morbidity can reach 100% but mortality is limited (under 10%), though secondary bacterial infection (Mycoplasma, E. coli) is common. Symptoms: abnormal breathing, gasping, coughing, and tracheal rattles in broilers/layers; in chicks it's more serious — conjunctivitis followed by nasal discharge and cheesy tracheal exudate that can cause suffocation; egg production can drop up to 50%, with misshapen/soft-shelled eggs and watery egg contents; there is no diarrhea and no nervous signs. Treatment: no specific cure, though a 5–7 day antibiotic course can help fight secondary bacterial infection. Prevention: an IB vaccine is often combined with the ND vaccine; unvaccinated chickens are susceptible, and effective prevention generally needs a structured program, mostly practical on commercial farms.
